The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the likelihood is factorized into independent factors, the posterior distribution can be obtained in a similar manner.
, when the likelihood factorizes into a product of functions of the data and the prior factorizes into a similar product, the posterior distribution factorizes into a corresponding product.
, in the case of monotone missing data, we can use standard results to obtain the posterior distribution without the need for numerical integration, which is a significant advantage.
